name: PenShot (story-shot-agent)
tagline: Breaks screenplays into shot lists and generates Sora/Veo/Runway-ready video prompts.
description: An LLM-powered agent that parses scripts in any format, performs shot-by-shot breakdowns, and emits coherent text-to-video prompts with cross-shot character consistency. Runs as an MCP server, Python SDK, REST API, or LangGraph node — the missing link between a screenplay and a generation pipeline.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add penshot -- python -m penshot.mcp_server --max-concurrent 5 --queue-size 500 (after pip install penshot)

auth.key_url: Bring your own LLM and embedding endpoints — set PENSHOT_LLM__DEFAULT__{BASE_URL,API_KEY,MODEL_NAME} and the matching PENSHOT_EMBED__DEFAULT__* vars; OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek and Ollama are named as working providers

notes: Still growing and genuinely active: 203 stars (up from 139 in five weeks), last commit 17 Sep 2026, PyPI 0.3.7 shipped 2 Sep 2026, MIT. Seven tools, read from the server source rather than the README — breakdown_script, get_task_status, get_task_result, cancel_task, list_tasks, get_queue_status, get_stats — and the install line now carries the --max-concurrent/--queue-size flags the project's own example config uses. THE CATCH THAT BITES: the stdio server advertises every tool with an empty JSON-Schema parameter block, so your client sees no argument names and you have to spell the arguments out in the prompt; the FastAPI surface in mcp_http_server.py has full parameter descriptions but it is a plain REST façade on :8000, not MCP over HTTP, so do not expect a remote_url. Setup is heavier than the one-line install suggests — an LLM endpoint, an embedding model and PENSHOT_REDIS_URL all have to be in .env first, or use the published ghcr.io/neopen/penshot image with docker compose. The maintainers still say it is optimized in depth for Chinese scripts with other languages 'in continuous iteration'. Async is the sane mode: submit with breakdown_script, poll get_task_status, collect get_task_result — and note task success reports as 'success', not 'completed'. Directory finding, still true: no dedicated MCP exists for Final Draft, Celtx, WriterDuet, or Fountain — script writing itself is best done with your agent directly (Fountain is plain text), stored via the Notion or Google Drive MCPs.

name: studio-state
tagline: Keeps AI-film characters, locations, shots, and lock status grounded in project files.
description: A stateless MCP server for long-running AI film and episodic projects: it reads a file-based show folder and tells an agent where the production stands. Its tools orient the session, report per-shot status, and write only a small sidecar when a shot is fired, locked, or needs rework.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add studio-state -e STUDIO_ROOT=/abs/path/your_show -- python3 /abs/path/studio-state-public/server.py

auth.key_url: Requires a local project folder containing _pipeline/STATE.json and episodes/

notes: MIT, still live but frozen: re-checked 20 Sep 2026 and the last push is unchanged at 16 Jun 2026 — three months without a commit — with still 0 stars, so treat it as one studio's shim published rather than a maintained project. The repo is not archived and INSTALL.md is still in place, so nothing has broken; nothing has moved either. Prerequisites the README front-loads: Python 3.9+ and `pip install "mcp[cli]"`, plus a project root containing _pipeline/STATE.json and episodes/ — run tests/test_acceptance.py against the bundled demo project first (expect 4/4). It is a state shim, not a generator, and the paid Studio Method pack is upsold in the README. The useful bit is safe by design — only `update_shot` writes, and only to a per-scene `shot_status.json` sidecar.

name: Miro MCP
tagline: Official Miro MCP — build and read storyboards, frames, and planning boards via AI.
description: Miro's hosted MCP server (public beta) lets agents create and read board content, now through an SVG canvas model: the agent writes a board by sending SVG and reads one back the same way, alongside tools to create and search boards, place images, and work prototypes and comments. A strong fit for storyboard layouts, shot-planning walls, and mood boards your whole team can see.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http miro https://mcp.miro.com

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; run /mcp auth in Claude Code and complete the Miro browser flow

notes: The tool surface was rebuilt since we last checked, so cached configs and prompts will break. Miro's tools page now documents an SVG canvas model — canvas_create_from_svg, canvas_read_as_svg, canvas_update_from_svg and a canvas_get_canvas_composer_skill helper — and states that board_list_items and the whole context_*, layout_*, diagram_* and doc_* families were removed; table_create, table_list_rows and table_sync_rows are marked deprecating soon. Practical effect for storyboards: you no longer place sticky notes and frames item by item, you hand the server SVG. Still public beta more than seven months after the 2 Feb 2026 launch — the Claude Code marketplace listing still says 'MCP is in Public Beta', even though developers.miro.com now leads with 'works for all Miro plans, even free teams'. Enterprise remains the catch: that listing says an Enterprise admin must enable MCP before anyone can authorize. Endpoint re-confirmed 20 Sep 2026 as https://mcp.miro.com (Miro's connect docs write it with a trailing slash; both forms are in Miro's own material). The Claude Code plugin route needs two commands, not one — /plugin marketplace add miroapp/miro-ai then /plugin install miro@miro-ai — and it ships three skills (miro-code-review, miro-code-spec, miro-code-explain-on-board) that are engineering-facing rather than film-facing. miroapp/miro-ai is alive: 154 stars, last push 17 Sep 2026. Tool names above are from developers.miro.com/docs/miro-mcp-tools — the server's own tools/list is the source of truth.

name: FrameThrower
tagline: Cinematography reference: search film stills from 5,489 films by lighting, lens, shot size, colour and mood.
description: A remote MCP server over one of the largest film still libraries on the internet — 5,489 films indexed frame by frame on lighting key and quality, lens character, shot size, camera angle, colour palette in hex, mood and era. An agent searches in plain language, narrows by craft attribute, and refines from any frame the user reacts to, which is the loop a director or DP actually works in when building a lookbook or shot list. Returns metadata, thumbnails, colour palettes and deep links — never raw image bytes, so it is a reference tool rather than a source of generation inputs.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http framethrower https://framethrower.ai/api/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth 2.1 — the client opens a FrameThrower sign-in; the agent then acts as that account. No API key.

notes: Endpoint, four tools, OAuth 2.1, credit pricing and the 5,489-film index all unchanged on re-check. Remote and hosted, so nothing to install or keep running. Free tier is $2 of credits on signup with no card; each tool call costs 2 credits at $1 = 1,000 credits, so $1 covers 500 calls, and credits do not expire; top-ups come in $20 packs. No rate limits — when credits run out the tool returns the balance rather than failing silently. Frames are shown at reduced resolution as references for commentary and study — rights remain with their owners, and the server never returns image bytes. One-vendor operation: the repo (framethrower-ai/framethrower-mcp) is a README pointing at the hosted endpoint and has not been touched since 12 Aug 2026, so there is no code to audit and no second maintainer if the service lapses. Submitted by the vendor.

name: FilmMap
tagline: Where films and series were actually shot: 15,000+ locations in 162 countries, from Wikidata.
description: A read-only remote MCP over a Wikidata-derived index of filming locations — 15,254 places across 162 countries, tied to 9,181 films and series plus 1,883 games and the indexed anime and manga. An agent can ask where a production was shot, what was shot at a given place, search by coordinates and radius, or rank the most-filmed locations in a country. For recce and reference it answers the question a location scout starts with: who has already shot here, and what did it look like on screen. No signup, no key, no install — point a client at the endpoint and query.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http filmmap https://thefilmmap.com/mcp

notes: Days old: the repo was created 2026-08-18 (MIT, 0 stars, one personal account, no commits since the day it landed) and the registry entry com.thefilmmap/filming-locations v1.1.0 was published 2026-08-21. Endpoint verified live on 2026-08-22 — a GET on https://thefilmmap.com/mcp returns 405, which is what a POST-only stateless streamable HTTP server should do. The docs publish a JSON client config rather than a per-client command; the claude mcp add line above is that endpoint in Claude Code form. Read the medium distinction before quoting anything: films and series carry real filming locations (Wikidata P915), while games, anime and manga carry narrative settings (P840) and were filmed nowhere, and the server labels each record so an agent does not conflate them. Coverage is honestly incomplete — 834 productions have no precise coordinates and 3,906 cannot be placed at all, listed publicly at thefilmmap.com/gaps/. A place is not a scene: there is no shot-level granularity, so this narrows a recce list, it does not replace one. Licensing is mixed — the dataset is CC0, but Wikipedia-sourced claims arrive separately labelled under CC BY-SA 4.0 and must be cited as such, and Commons photographs keep their own terms. The counts also disagree with themselves: the repo blurb says 15,272 locations and 12,762 productions where the data page says 15,254 and breaks the productions down differently.
